paragraphs.en: Mr. Bennet was among the earliest of those who waited on Mr. Bingley. He had always intended to visit him, though to the last always assuring his wife that he should not go; and till the evening after the visit was paid she had no knowledge of it. It was then disclosed in the following manner. Observing his second daughter employed in trimming a hat, he suddenly addressed her with,--
paragraphs.zh: 班纳特先生是最早去拜访宾利先生的人之一。他一直打算去拜访他，尽管直到最后还一直向妻子保证他不会去；直到拜访之后的晚上，他妻子才知道这件事。事情是这样被揭露的：他看到次女正在装饰一顶帽子，突然对她说道——

paragraphs.en: “I hope Mr. Bingley will like it, Lizzy.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望宾利先生会喜欢它，丽齐。”

paragraphs.en: “We are not in a way to know _what_ Mr. Bingley likes,” said her mother, resentfully, “since we are not to visit.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们根本无从知道班纳利先生喜欢什么，”她母亲不满地说，“因为我们不能去拜访。”

paragraphs.en: “But you forget, mamma,” said Elizabeth, “that we shall meet him at the assemblies, and that Mrs. Long has promised to introduce him.”
paragraphs.zh: “可是你忘了，妈妈，”伊丽莎白说，“我们在舞会上会见到他的，朗太太已经答应介绍他了。”

paragraphs.en: “I do not believe Mrs. Long will do any such thing. She has two nieces of her own. She is a selfish, hypocritical woman, and I have no opinion of her.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不相信朗太太会做这种事。她自己有两个侄女。她是个自私虚伪的女人，我对她毫无好感。”

paragraphs.en: “No more have I,” said Mr. Bennet; “and I am glad to find that you do not depend on her serving you.”
paragraphs.zh: “我也没有了，”班纳特先生说，“很高兴发现你并不依赖她来伺候你。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Bennet deigned not to make any reply; but, unable to contain herself, began scolding one of her daughters.
paragraphs.zh: 班纳特太太不屑于做任何回答，但她忍不住，开始责骂她的其中一个女儿。

paragraphs.en: “Don’t keep coughing so, Kitty, for heaven’s sake! Have a little compassion on my nerves. You tear them to pieces.”
paragraphs.zh: “别那么咳个没完，基蒂，看在上帝的份上！你至少得怜悯一下我的神经。你把它们都撕得粉碎。”

paragraphs.en: “Kitty has no discretion in her coughs,” said her father; “she times them ill.”
paragraphs.zh: “凯蒂咳嗽的时候毫无分寸，”她的父亲说，“她总是选错时间。”

paragraphs.en: “I do not cough for my own amusement,” replied Kitty, fretfully. “When is your next ball to be, Lizzy?”
paragraphs.zh: “我咳嗽可不是为了自己取乐，”凯蒂烦躁地回答，“莉齐，你们下一场舞会是什么时候？”

paragraphs.en: “To-morrow fortnight.”
paragraphs.zh: “后两周。”

paragraphs.en: “Ay, so it is,” cried her mother, “and Mrs. Long does not come back till the day before; so, it will be impossible for her to introduce him, for she will not know him herself.”
paragraphs.zh: “啊，原来是这样，”她母亲喊道，“洛太太要到前一天才回来，所以她不可能介绍他，因为她自己也不认识他。”

paragraphs.en: “Then, my dear, you may have the advantage of your friend, and introduce Mr. Bingley to _her_.”
paragraphs.zh: “那么，亲爱的，你就可以占朋友的便宜，把宾利先生介绍给她。”

paragraphs.en: “Impossible, Mr. Bennet, impossible, when I am not acquainted with him myself; how can you be so teasing?”
paragraphs.zh: “不可能，班纳特先生，不可能，我自己还不认识他呢，你怎么这么爱开玩笑？”

paragraphs.en: “I honour your circumspection. A fortnight’s acquaintance is certainly very little. One cannot know what a man really is by the end of a fortnight. But if _we_ do not venture, somebody else will; and after all, Mrs. Long and her nieces must stand their chance; and, therefore, as she will think it an act of kindness, if you decline the office, I will take it on myself.”
paragraphs.zh: “我钦佩你的谨慎。两周的相识当然非常短暂，一个人不可能在两周结束时就被真正了解。但是，如果我们不主动，别人就会这么做；况且，朗太太和她的侄女们也必须面对她们的机遇；因此，如果你拒绝这个职务，她会认为这是出于善意，那么我将自己来承担这个责任。”

paragraphs.en: The girls stared at their father. Mrs. Bennet said only, “Nonsense, nonsense!”
paragraphs.zh: 姑娘们盯着她们的父亲。班纳特太太只说：“胡说，胡说！”

paragraphs.en: “What can be the meaning of that emphatic exclamation?” cried he. “Do you consider the forms of introduction, and the stress that is laid on them, as nonsense? I cannot quite agree with you _there_. What say you, Mary? For you are a young lady of deep reflection, I know, and read great books, and make extracts.”
paragraphs.zh: “那句强调的感叹话又是什么意思呢？”他喊道，“你认为介绍的形式以及对它们的强调都是无意义的吗？我不能完全同意你的看法——这点。玛丽，你怎么看？我知道你是个善于深思的年轻女士，读过很多书，还做读书摘录。”

paragraphs.en: Mary wished to say something very sensible, but knew not how.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽想说一些非常明智的话，但不知道如何表达。

paragraphs.en: “While Mary is adjusting her ideas,” he continued, “let us return to Mr. Bingley.”
paragraphs.zh: “当玛丽在调整她的想法时，”他继续说道，“我们还是回到宾利先生吧。”

paragraphs.en: “I am sick of Mr. Bingley,” cried his wife.
paragraphs.zh: “我受够了宾利先生了，”他妻子喊道。

paragraphs.en: “I am sorry to hear _that_; but why did you not tell me so before? If I had known as much this morning, I certainly would not have called on him. It is very unlucky; but as I have actually paid the visit, we cannot escape the acquaintance now.”
paragraphs.zh: “我听到这个消息很遗憾；但是你为什么之前不告诉我呢？如果我早上知道这一点，我肯定不会去拜访他。这真是不幸运；但既然我已经拜访过了，我们现在就无法避免和他认识了。”

paragraphs.en: The astonishment of the ladies was just what he wished--that of Mrs. Bennet perhaps surpassing the rest; though when the first tumult of joy was over, she began to declare that it was what she had expected all the while.
paragraphs.zh: 这些女士们的惊讶正是他所希望的——尤其是班纳特太太的惊讶或许超过了其他人；不过当最初的喜悦情绪平息下来后，她开始声称这正是她一直所预料的。

paragraphs.en: “How good it was in you, my dear Mr. Bennet! But I knew I should persuade you at last. I was sure you loved your girls too well to neglect such an acquaintance. Well, how pleased I am! And it is such a good joke, too, that you should have gone this morning, and never said a word about it till now.”
paragraphs.zh: “亲爱的本内特先生，你真是太好了！但我知道我最终会说服你的。我确信你非常爱你的女儿们，不会忽视这样一种结识的机会。嗯，我真是太高兴了！这真是个好笑的事，你今天早上去了，却直到现在才说一句话。”

paragraphs.en: “Now, Kitty, you may cough as much as you choose,” said Mr. Bennet; and, as he spoke, he left the room, fatigued with the raptures of his wife.
paragraphs.zh: “现在，基蒂，你想咳嗽就尽管咳吧，”班纳特先生说；他说着，便离开了房间，他已被妻子的兴奋情绪弄得筋疲力尽。

paragraphs.en: “What an excellent father you have, girls,” said she, when the door was shut. “I do not know how you will ever make him amends for his kindness; or me either, for that matter. At our time of life, it is not so pleasant, I can tell you, to be making new acquaintances every day; but for your sakes we would do anything. Lydia, my love, though you _are_ the youngest, I dare say Mr. Bingley will dance with you at the next ball.”
paragraphs.zh: “你们有一个多好的父亲啊，姑娘们，”门关上后她说道，“我不知道你们将来怎么报答他的恩情；或者说，我也是一样。到了我们这个年纪，每天结识新朋友可不太愉快，我告诉你吧；但为了你们，我们什么都愿意做。丽迪雅，我亲爱的，虽然你是最小的，但我敢说宾利先生下次舞会一定会和你跳舞。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” said Lydia, stoutly, “I am not afraid; for though I _am_ the youngest, I’m the tallest.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”莉迪亚坚定地说，“我不害怕；虽然我是最小的，但我最高。”

paragraphs.en: The rest of the evening was spent in conjecturing how soon he would return Mr. Bennet’s visit, and determining when they should ask him to dinner.
paragraphs.zh: 剩下的夜晚都是在猜测他何时会回访班纳特先生，以及商定何时邀请他共进晚餐。
